record.short: Free plan loses its Brain² trial of 500 credits per workspace; AI features now show Not included on Free.
record.headline: ClickUp now limits AI to paid plans: the Free plan’s Brain² trial with 500 credits per workspace is gone and its AI features are marked Not included.
rows: Every plan ships with ClickUp Brain²
record.who: Workspaces on the Free plan; paid plans keep their pooled monthly AI credit allowances.
record.read: AI is being positioned as a paid-plan benefit, which pushes free workspaces to upgrade to try Brain². This is an inference from the page copy changing from every plan to paid plans.
record.caveat: Based on the pricing page and comparison table only; no announcement was found.

record.deltaSub: Free plan block storage, solo workspaces
record.headline: Notion’s FAQ now says every Free Plan workspace has a block limit, where a Free workspace used by one person could previously add as many pages and blocks as it liked.
record.who: People using the Free plan on their own; multi-member Free workspaces already had a limit.
record.read: This tightens the free tier for solo users and nudges heavy personal users toward a paid plan. It is an inference from the FAQ wording alone.
record.caveat: Only the FAQ text changed; the page gives no limit figure, date or enforcement details.

items.why: The free Basic plan now lists a cap of up to 10 guides created and shared; the earlier page listed no cap. Enterprise feature list was also reshuffled with no price change.

record.short: The free Basic plan now lists a limit: create and share up to 10 guides.
record.deltaSub: Free plan guides created and shared
record.headline: Scribe’s pricing page now states that the free Basic plan lets users create and share up to 10 guides, a limit the earlier page did not list.
record.who: Free Basic users; the page does not say whether existing free accounts are capped.
record.read: A visible cap on the free plan turns it into a trial-style funnel toward paid seats. This is our interpretation of the added feature line.
record.caveat: The earlier page listed no limit, so this may be a new cap or a limit that was newly disclosed.
